The stone keep and walls of Guimarães Castle
From Porto · one day out
Day trips from Porto. Pick one, maybe two.
Northern Portugal is compact: most of these are an hour or two away. With three or four days in Porto, one day out is plenty. Choose by what you came for — wine, old towns, the sea, or a walk.
Douro Valley — wine and terraces
The classic, and the longest day. Train, tour or car compared in detail on our

The classic Douro day
Two tastings, a traditional lunch and an hour on the river. The most-booked Douro day on GetYourGuide.
Via Amarante and the Galafura view
Amarante’s old bridge, the viewpoint over the whole valley, lunch, a tasting and a boat at Pinhão.
Braga and Guimarães — where Portugal started
Guimarães has the castle and a medieval centre; Braga has the cathedral and the Bom Jesus stairway above the town. Together they make one well-paced day. Full guide:
Minibus with a guide: Braga cathedral, Bom Jesus do Monte, Braga’s old centre, then Guimarães castle and the old town. Option with or without monument tickets.
The same day, small group
The same two towns with a smaller group, for people who would rather not share a coach.
Adding Viana do Castelo
Braga and Guimarães plus Viana do Castelo on the coast — a long day, three towns.
Aveiro and Costa Nova — canals and striped houses
South of Porto: canals with painted moliceiro boats, art nouveau façades, then the striped beach houses of Costa Nova. Flat and easy — a good day with children or after the Douro. Full guide:
Aveiro’s centre and canals, then Costa Nova by the sea.
Aveiro with a boat ride
Aveiro, Costa Nova and the Senhor da Pedra chapel on the beach at Miramar.
For walkers
Paiva walkways and the 516 Arouca bridge
Wooden walkways along the Paiva river and one of the longest pedestrian suspension bridges in the world. Not for vertigo.
Peneda-Gerês National Park
Portugal’s only national park: granite villages, streams and waterfalls. Bring shoes you can get wet.

What is the best day trip from Porto?
For wine and landscape, the Douro Valley. For history, Braga and Guimarães together. For something easy and flat by the sea, Aveiro and Costa Nova.
Can I do Braga and Guimarães in one day from Porto?
Yes. Both are under an hour from Porto and organised day trips usually combine them. Trains also run from Porto to each town, but doing both by train in one day is tight.

Is a food tour in Porto worth it?
On your first day, yes: you learn what to order — francesinha, bifana, petiscos, tinned fish, pastel de nata — and where locals actually eat, which pays off for the rest of the trip.
What should I eat in Porto?
A francesinha once, a bifana standing up, grilled fish near the coast in Matosinhos, tinned fish, and a glass of port or vinho verde with petiscos.

Francisco Sá Carneiro Airport (OPO)
From Porto airport to your bed, without overthinking it.
Porto’s airport is close and on the metro. For most people the metro is the answer. A pre-booked driver earns its price late at night, with children, or with more bags than hands.
Four ways in
Metro, taxi, transfer, car
1. Metro, line E (violet).

From the station at arrivals to Trindade in about half an hour; change there for São Bento or Gaia. Buy a rechargeable Andante card at the machines. It does not run all night — check the last train if you land late.

From the rank or pick-up zone outside arrivals. Fine for two people with luggage.
4. Pre-booked transfer.
A driver with your name in arrivals, a fixed price agreed before you fly. The calm choice for a late landing, a family, or a group.

How do I get from Porto airport to the city centre?
Metro line E (violet) runs from the airport to Trindade in central Porto in about half an hour. Taxis and ride-hailing wait outside arrivals, and pre-booked transfers meet you inside.
Can I get from Porto airport to Póvoa de Varzim by metro?
Yes. Take line E and change at Verdes to line B (red) toward Póvoa de Varzim. Vila do Conde is on the same line.
Port wine cellars in Gaia: which one to book | Day in Portugal
Which port wine cellar to visit in Vila Nova de Gaia: Taylor’s, Cálem, Cockburn’s, Fonseca, Burmester or Poças. What each visit is like, and where to book a timed slot.
Port cellars in Gaia — which one to book
A guide beside a large port-wine vat inside the Cálem cellars in Vila Nova de Gaia
Vila Nova de Gaia · port wine
One port cellar in Gaia is enough. Pick the right one.

The lodges sit across the river from Ribeira, a walk over the lower deck of the Dom Luís I bridge. They all explain the same process — grapes from the Douro, ageing in Gaia — so choose by the kind of visit, not the brand. In summer, book a time; walk-ins wait.
Near the river, easy to reach
The big names
Cálem: short, guided, by the water
On the riverfront itself, so no climb. A guided visit through the museum and cellars, ending with a tasting. Good if you have one hour and no plan.
Cálem with fado in the evening
The same cellar visit, then a short live fado set with a glass. A gentler evening than a full fado dinner.
Taylor’s: self-paced, up the hill
An audio-guided walk through a centuries-old lodge, then a tasting, with gardens and a view back over Porto. The lanes up from the river are steep.
Taylor’s plus the WOW museums
Taylor’s with WOW, the wine and culture quarter next door — more tastings, a longer afternoon. Also listed on GetYourGuide as a Taylor’s audio-guide ticket.
Taylor’s on its own on GetYourGuide:
Taylor’s winery tour with audio guide
Quieter tastings
If you would rather not be in a group of forty
Cockburn’s: a working lodge
One of the largest lodges in Gaia, with a cooperage where the barrels are still repaired. A guided visit and tasting.
Fonseca: self-guided, then taste
Go round at your own pace and finish with a tasting. For people who prefer reading the walls to following a guide.
Burmester: small house, guided tasting
A smaller lodge on the riverfront with a guided visit and tasting. The same house is the optional cellar on the six-bridges cruise on our
booking page
Poças: family-run since 1918
An independent, family-owned port house, still Portuguese-owned. Visit and tasting.

the Gaia cable car runs along the riverfront to the top of the bridge — handy after a tasting.

Do I need to book a port cellar tour in Gaia in advance?
In July to September, yes: walk-in slots at the big lodges often mean a long wait or a later time. Out of season you can usually walk in, but a booked slot still saves the queue.
Which Gaia port cellar is best for a first visit?

Pick by what you want: Taylor’s for a self-paced visit with a view, Cálem for a short guided tour near the river (with a fado option), Cockburn’s for a big working lodge, or a small house such as Poças or Burmester for a quieter tasting.
